To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

climate models project an increase in the annual streamflow in the four Ethiopian rivers, but the observed trends in precipitation over Ethiopia contradict such projected increase in annual streamflow.

the ensemble median of 10 GCM projections projects the temperature in Ethiopia to increase by about 2.3 (3.3) °C in the 2051–2070 period (2071–2101 period), whereas the mean precipitation is projected to decrease by about − 1% (− 4%) in the same periods.
the projected climate change impacts on the streamflow in the major river basins of Ethiopia are not consistent with the observed climate trends in recent decades.

the projected increase in the annual streamflow in Ethiopia is likely to be less than the projected increase in mean annual precipitation due to climate change.

climate change is likely to increase the annual streamflow in the four study river basins in the future, but the increase is likely to be smaller than the projected increase in mean annual precipitation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the projected increase in streamflow in the 2051–2070 and 2071-2100 periods is not consistent with the observed decrease in streamflow during the last 40 years.
the projected climate change in the four study basins is likely to increase the mean annual streamflows of all the four basins, except Genale river.
future streamflow projections should be used with caution, especially for the 2050 period, as they may not be consistent with the observed climate change trends in recent decades.
